parameters.content:
## Setup required: Telegram chat ID (always, no exceptions)

This workflow is cron-triggered, *i.e.*, there is no incoming Telegram message to derive a chat ID from, so the placeholder `YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` in its Telegram node MUST be replaced with a real value before it can send anything at all, in every run, not just for testing.

**How to find your chat ID:**
1. Message this template's bot at least once (any text).
2. Open **JobOps Template Bot Router** → click the **JobOps Template Bot Trigger** node → **Listen for test event**.
3. Send another message to the bot.
4. n8n captures the incoming update — find `message.chat.id` in the output panel. That's your chat ID.
5. Paste it into the `YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` field in the Send Reviews Digest node.

**Important:** this workflow is left published/live with the placeholder still in place. 
It will run on its schedule and fail (harmlessly) until you fill in a real ID. 
After editing the chat ID field, you must **republish this workflow** for the change to take effect. 
Editing alone only updates the draft, not what's actually running.

## Setup required: jobops_template_config Data Table ID (always, no exceptions)

This workflow looks up the Airtable base/table IDs it needs from an n8n Data Table (D-24) rather than hardcoding them or using n8n Variables (gated behind a paid plan). The placeholder `YOUR_JOBOPS_TEMPLATE_CONFIG_DATA_TABLE_ID` in the **Load Config** node MUST be replaced with your own Data Table's ID before this workflow can do anything, in every run, not just for testing.

**How to set it up:**
1. Create a Data Table in your n8n instance (Data Tables → New), name it `jobops_template_config`.
2. Add one row with a column for every base/table ID your own Airtable base uses (e.g. baseId, tableReviews).
3. Open the **Load Config** node in this workflow → click into the Data Table field → select your new table. This replaces the placeholder with your table's real ID.

**Important:** this workflow is left published/live with the placeholder still in place. It will run on its schedule and fail (harmlessly) until you fill in your real Data Table ID. After editing it, you must **republish this workflow** for the change to take effect — editing alone only updates the draft, not what's actually running.

nodes.name: Setup Note - Config Data Table ID

parameters.content:
## Setup required: jobops_template_reviews_digests Data Table ID (always, no exceptions)

This workflow stores a mapping from the sent digest message's Telegram ID to the Reviews record it belongs to (D-22), so a reply to the digest can be matched back to the right record by **JobOps Template - Reviews Reply Capture**. The placeholder `YOUR_JOBOPS_TEMPLATE_REVIEWS_DIGESTS_DATA_TABLE_ID` in the **Store Digest Message Link** node MUST be replaced with your own Data Table's ID before this workflow can do anything, in every run, not just for testing.

**How to set it up:**
1. Create a second Data Table in your n8n instance, name it `jobops_template_reviews_digests`, with columns `messageId` and `reviewsRecordId`.
2. Open the **Store Digest Message Link** node → click into the Data Table field → select your new table. This replaces the placeholder with your table's real ID.
3. Use the same table's ID in **JobOps Template - Reviews Reply Capture**'s **Lookup Digest Record** node — both workflows must point at the same table.

**Important:** this workflow is left published/live with the placeholder still in place. It will run on its schedule and fail (harmlessly) until you fill in your real Data Table ID. After editing it, you must **republish this workflow** for the change to take effect — editing alone only updates the draft, not what's actually running.
